rfm_tuples.R: We were in full compliance with these covenants and restrictions as of December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify covenant compliance via senior credit facility disclosures and check whether covenants are described as 'maintenance of certain financial ratios' without disclosing actual leverage ratio or headroom (Mode B: investor cannot recompute cushion).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 8 + Item 7 Liquidity; senior credit agreement (seventh amended)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Compliant per management; no quantitative covenant headroom disclosed. Senior credit agreement bears variable-rate SOFR-based interest; $986.6M total debt, 54% of total capitalization; $581.4M revolver availability at 12/31/23; $24.3M cash on hand. Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-04-25) repeats 'in full compliance' language.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Compliance claim is reaffirmed in subsequent 10-Q; sizable $581M revolver headroom and PwC unqualified opinion. Mode B: lack of quantitative covenant cushion is typical for non-distressed IG-style credit and not a red flag at this size.

rfm_tuples.R: In February 2024, the Company repaid the $70.0 million then outstanding of the 2.625% Notes through borrowings on our revolving credit facility. Accordingly, we have classified the 2.625% Notes as long-term obligations as of the December 31, 2023 balance sheet date.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the refinancing actually closed and revolver capacity supports it (Mode A); Mode B: check that the refinancing was not a 'distressed exchange' or covenant-driven amendment (look for amendment fee, increased pricing, or new restrictions).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 + Note 8 'Subsequent Events'; senior credit agreement (seventh amended and restated)
rfm_tuples.M_value: $70M maturity was refinanced via revolver at par; $581.4M revolver availability provides ~8x coverage of the maturity. No reported amendment, fee, or pricing step-up. Q1 2024 10-Q confirms note retired and covenant compliance maintained.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Routine refinancing of a 2024 convert at par from existing revolver capacity. This is the OPPOSITE of distressed refinancing (no exchange offer, no PIK toggle, no equity component, no covenant amendment).

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2023, we had $986.6 million of debt outstanding, representing 54% of total capitalization... approximately 29% of our products when measured in terms of revenues, are sterilized by third-party sterilizers using ethylene oxide.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm debt/cap ratio against balance sheet (long-term debt $973.1M + current $0.7M = $973.8M debt vs equity ~$830M). Mode B: 29% EtO exposure is material; check whether disclosed litigation overlap exists.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Consolidated Balance Sheet; Item 1A Risk Factors; Item 3 Legal Proceedings
rfm_tuples.M_value: Balance-sheet debt and capitalization roughly reconcile. EtO exposure flows into Cobb County Action and Douglas County Action (personal injury). Cobb County: motion to dismiss precluded employee claims under workers' comp; remaining plaintiffs filed voluntary dismissal without prejudice with refile deadline of June 2024 (pre-cutoff disclosed). Chubb (insurer) ruled in favor of CONMED on coverage in March 2022; one insurer is providing coverage for certain claims.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Leverage is real but serviceable; EtO litigation is disclosed honestly with specific procedural posture, named courts, named insurers, and adverse-decision visibility. This is high-quality disclosure, not obscured distress.

rfm_tuples.R: Net sales were $1,244.7 million in 2023, up 19.1% (1.8% FX, 20.9% constant currency)... net income was $64.5 million in 2023 vs net loss of $(80.6) million in 2022.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify revenue and EPS trajectory year over year. Mode B: check that 2022 loss is explained and that growth is organic vs acquisition-bought.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 2022 net loss of $(80.6)M was driven by $51.6M Biorez goodwill plus $138.5M In2Bones goodwill creating fair-value step-up amortization, plus convertible notes hedge transaction settlement costs ($5.5M) and 2.625% Notes extinguishment loss. 2023 returned to $64.5M net income. Q1 2024 10-Q: sales $312.3M vs $295.5M Q1 2023 = +5.7% reported (+8.0% general surgery). Operating cash flow $125.3M in 2023 vs $33.4M in 2022 - inflected positive.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Recovery is real and broadly disclosed. Growth comes from underlying surgical procedure volume + AirSeal/BioBrace/Buffalo Filter franchises plus 2022 acquisition contributions, not accounting tricks.

rfm_tuples.R: We are not a party to any pending legal proceedings other than ordinary routine litigation incidental to our business (Item 3 boilerplate) - notwithstanding which the company discloses Cobb County and Douglas County EtO Actions in Note 14.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: check whether boilerplate 'no material legal proceedings' is contradicted elsewhere in the filing (a classic disclosure-evasion pattern), and whether contingent loss reserves were quantified.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Item 3 uses boilerplate but Note 14 provides detailed disclosure of Cobb County Action (personal injury EtO claims) including motion-to-dismiss ruling, Northern District of NY coverage litigation against Chubb (CONMED won March 10, 2022, on Cobb coverage; one insurer covering some claims), voluntary dismissal of remaining Cobb plaintiffs with June 2024 refile deadline. Italy medical-device tax also disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Item 3 boilerplate is technically misleading given the disclosed EtO actions, but Note 14 cures the gap with specific facts. Modest disclosure quality issue, not material obscuring of distress.

rfm_tuples.R: The fair value of contingent consideration at December 31, 2023 was $41.4 million for the In2Bones acquisition and $128.8 million for the Biorez acquisition... we expect to finance contingent consideration payments related to our Biorez and In2Bones acquisitions in whole or in part through borrowings on our revolving credit facility.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: total earnout liability is $170.2M with revolver as funding source. Verify implied stress on liquidity if both earnouts hit max value, and whether PwC flagged the valuation as a Critical Audit Matter.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 3 (Acquisitions); Note 5/6 (Fair Value); PwC Report (Critical Audit Matter)
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC identified contingent consideration as a Critical Audit Matter (CAM) due to (i) management judgment on revenue volatilities and discount rates, (ii) high auditor subjectivity. Earnout funding via revolver leaves ~$411M revolver headroom after max payout - still comfortable but a real claim on liquidity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed appropriately as a CAM. Honest quantification of liability with named funding source. Mode B does not catch obscuring - on the contrary, the disclosure quality is strong.

rfm_tuples.R: We have served as the Company's auditor since 1982. /s/ PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Fairport, New York, February 28, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm Big 4 auditor with long tenure and no resignation, going-concern qualification, or restatement. Mode B: check for any change in audit partner or scope.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC, 42-year tenure (1982 to 2024), unqualified opinion on financials AND on internal control over financial reporting. CAM disclosed (contingent consideration). No going-concern paragraph. No disagreements.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Big 4 with multi-decade tenure and clean dual opinion is the strongest possible auditor signal. The opposite of the 'small-cap auditor degradation' pattern seen in true distress names.

rfm_tuples.R: Item 5 / 10b5-1: The Company paid a quarterly dividend of $0.20 per share in 2022 and 2023 and the fourth quarter dividend for 2023 was paid on January 5, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: check insider behavior vs the stock drawdown (CNMD was down ~45% from trailing 52w high at 2024-05-15). Are insiders selling into weakness (bearish) or buying (bullish)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Sampled 2024 Form 4s: May 14, 2024 - Bronson, Director, OPEN-MARKET PURCHASE (code P) 1,350 sh @ $72.09; May 8, 2024 - Aronson, Director, PURCHASE 2,000 sh @ $70.98; May 2, 2024 - Beyer, Director, PURCHASE 3,000 sh @ $68.30; April 26 - Beyer received 20,060-share grant (code A). 2023 Form 4s: execs (Peters, Garner) sold via systematic 10b5-1 at $100+ before drawdown.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: VERY STRONG bullish insider signal: multiple independent directors making open-market purchases at $68-$72 in early May 2024, immediately into the drawdown. This is the diametric opposite of the 'insiders dump into distress' pattern. Indicates board confidence that the drawdown is overdone.

rfm_tuples.R: Loans under our senior credit agreement bear interest based on SOFR... interest rates rose in fiscal year 2023 and may rise further going forward.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify interest expense trajectory and disclosure of rate sensitivity. Mode B: confirm interest coverage is not deteriorating into covenant pressure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7A Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures; Statements of Operations
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disclosed: $116.6M variable-rate debt; 100bp rise = $1.2M annual interest expense impact - small relative to $1.24B revenue. Q1 2024 10-Q states interest expense DECREASED in Q1 2024 vs Q1 2023 due to lower weighted-average borrowings.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Interest sensitivity is quantified, sensitivity is small, and Q1 2024 already shows lower interest expense. No covenant-headroom concern.

rfm_tuples.R: Q1 2024 10-Q: Orthopedic surgery +2.9% to $134.9M, General surgery +8.0% to $177.4M, consolidated +5.7% to $312.3M (vs FY2023 +19.1%).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: claim evolution between FY2023 10-K (Feb 28, 2024) and Q1 2024 10-Q (April 25, 2024). Is growth decelerating sharply post-FY guidance?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Reported deceleration from +19.1% FY2023 to +5.7% Q1 2024 (note: 2023 had heavy acquisition contribution from Biorez/In2Bones rolling off comp). Q1 2024 orthopedic growth still positive at +2.9%, general surgery healthy at +8.0%. Net income remained positive. Covenant compliance reaffirmed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Growth has decelerated as the acquisition-driven 2023 comp anniversaries, but growth remains positive on both segments. No revenue decline, no margin collapse, no covenant tension. This is normal post-acquisition normalization, not deteriorating fundamentals.

supplemental_signals.free_cash_flow: Operating cash flow $125.3M in 2023 (vs $33.4M in 2022); reaccelerating

summary: CONMED is a mid-cap medical device manufacturer ($1.24B revenue, 54% surgical orthopedic/46% general surgery) with a clean Big 4 audit relationship (PwC, 42-year tenure, unqualified ICFR opinion, CAM only for routine contingent-consideration valuation), no going-concern language, no covenant amendments, and the February 2024 maturity of its 2.625% converts refinanced at par via $581M revolver capacity. The 45% drawdown into 2024-05-15 appears driven by post-acquisition growth deceleration (FY2023 +19.1% normalizing to Q1 2024 +5.7%) and broad medical-device sector multiple compression - NOT by any distress signal in the disclosures. Insiders are buying open-market in May 2024 (Bronson, Aronson, Beyer at $68-72) - a strong bullish counter-signal that argues management views the drawdown as a multiple-compression overshoot rather than a fundamental deterioration. The Item 3 boilerplate that contradicts Note 14 EtO litigation disclosure is the only modest disclosure-quality knock. This is a LONG-tier honest distressed-multiple name, not a SHORT-tier liar.
